Person who writes for a newspaper, magazine or news site — Periodista.
Extreme shortage of food in a region — Hambruna.
A great shortage of anything — Escasez.
There is a famine of good news.
Not the same as hunger, which one person can feel.
Bring someone back to consciousness — Reanimar / revivir.
Bring something back into use — Resucitar / recuperar.
The town revived an old festival.
Begin or start — Comenzar / dar comienzo.
The ceremony will commence at noon.
v|Formal. In everyday speech people say start or begin.
An observant child spotted the mistake.
Recognise who or what something is — Identificar.
She identified the man in the photograph.
Feel that you understand someone — Identificarse con.
Move from one place to another to live or work — Migrar / emigrar.
Workers migrate to the city in winter.
Travel to another region with the seasons — Migrar.
v|Noun: migration. A person who moves is a migrant.
A ship or large boat — Buque / embarcación.
A fishing vessel entered the port.
A container for liquid — Recipiente / vasija.
Pour the milk into a clean vessel.
A tube that carries blood — Vaso sanguíneo.
The doctor examined the blood vessels.
The ship meaning is formal or nautical.
Keep doing something in spite of difficulty — Persistir / insistir.
He persisted until the door opened.
Misty and not clear — Brumoso/a / con neblina.
The mountains looked hazy this morning.
My memory of that day is hazy.
A faint beam of light — Destello / resplandor.
A gleam of light came under the door.
Person who prepares and corrects writing for publication — Editor(a) / redactor(a).
The editor cut two pages from the article.
Verb: edit. False friend: a book publisher is a publisher, not an editor.
Hard to control; badly behaved — Revoltoso/a / indisciplinado/a.
The teacher calmed the unruly class.
Often used of crowds, children and hair.
Person competing for the same thing — Rival / competidor(a).
Be as good as someone else — Rivalizar con / competir con.
No team rivals them for speed.
Using strong physical force to hurt — Violento/a.
Very strong and sudden — Violento/a / intenso/a.
A violent storm hit the coast.
Cruel and without pity — Brutal / despiadado/a.
He gave me his brutal opinion.
Person on the other side of a fight, game or argument — Oponente / adversario/a / rival.
A noisy fight in a public place — Riña / pelea.
A brawl started outside the bar.
Two men brawled in the street.
An exact copy — Duplicado / copia exacta.
Keep a duplicate of the contract.
Make an exact copy of — Duplicar / copiar.
Do the same thing again needlessly — Duplicar esfuerzos.
v|As a noun the ending sounds like -kat, as a verb like -keit.
A vicious dog guarded the yard.
Turning round and round very fast — Girando / dando vueltas.
From the verb whirl: whirls, whirled, whirled.
The one expected to lose — El que lleva las de perder / el menos favorito.
Push with sudden force — Empujar con fuerza / clavar.
He thrust the key into the lock.
A strong push, noun — Empujón / embestida.
The thrust of the engine lifted the rocket.
Become or make larger — Expandir(se) / ampliar.
Metal expands when it is heated.
Say more about something — Ampliar / desarrollar.
Could you expand on that idea?
Make or become different — Alterar / modificar.
We altered the plan at the last minute.
Change clothes to fit — Arreglar / ajustar.
v|Careful: alter is to change, altar is a table in a church.
A mature tree gives good shade.
Behaving in a sensible adult way — Maduro/a / sensato/a.
She is very mature for her age.
The cheese matures for six months.
Treated with great respect — Sagrado/a / intocable.
Sunday lunch is sacred in my family.
Note the pronunciation: two syllables, SAY-krid.
Change something to make it better or newer — Revisar / corregir.
The author revised the last chapter.
I had to revise my opinion of him.
He made a pledge to help.
They pledged to finish the work.
Not planned; by chance — Casual / fortuito/a.
It was a casual meeting in the street.
Not permanent, of work — Eventual / temporal.
He found casual work in a bar.
We were fortunate to find a taxi.
Person who goes first and opens the way for others — Pionero/a.
She was a pioneer of modern surgery.
Be the first to do something — Ser pionero/a en.
They pioneered the use of solar power.
Thin in an attractive way — Delgado/a / esbelto/a.
They won by a slender margin.
Do better or be greater than — Superar / sobrepasar.
Extremely large in area or amount — Vasto/a / inmenso/a.
The amount something can hold — Capacidad / aforo.
The hall has a capacity of 500.
Ability to do something — Capacidad / aptitud.
He has a great capacity for work.
Go into or through something — Penetrar / atravesar.
The light penetrated the thick curtains.
Make a hole through something sharp — Perforar / agujerear.
Go through sound or light — Atravesar / rasgar.
The clock is accurate to the second.
Instrument that makes tiny things look bigger — Microscopio.
We looked at the cells under a microscope.
I am grateful for your help.
Pattern: grateful to someone for something. Noun: gratitude.
Very careful; avoiding risks — Cauteloso/a / prudente.
Be cautious on the wet road.
Sure of yourself or of something — Seguro/a / confiado/a.
She is confident about the exam.
Noun: confidence. Careful: a confidant is a person you trust with secrets.
